style.architecture: TEA with Browser.element: Main holds { form, companion }, one update, one view; GotForm / GotCompanion wrap each module's Msg (Html.map)
style.components: one Form module with one flat Model record (a field per state field) and one Msg (a constructor per control), a case branch per message with the ops as record updates; a Companion module; Ui's generic helpers (widget, when, option, nextId, toggleDone, andMap, onNumberInput)
style.types: int Int, bool Bool, text and enum String (options as data in the view and in a case for cycle), list a List of a type alias per list built by its positional constructor
style.derived: computed in view; an if is a let binding of the view function
style.viewSplit: the form is flat: view is Ui.widget … (List.concat [ viewX model, … ]) with a view function per field unit, named after its main field, returning List (Html Msg) and taking the whole form Model (units read earlier fields from anywhere); a unit's wrapper inline
style.lazy: none: the form is one record changing on every message, so lazy on the whole model never hits and per-unit field threading is not what an expert writes
style.decoder: Decode.succeed Model |> Ui.andMap (Decode.field ...) per field beyond Decode.map8
style.conditionals: a view function per conditional section, called as Ui.when condition (viewSection model), which renders an empty text node while the condition fails
style.crossReads: the view takes the Model of each widget it reads, before its own
style.lists: Html.Keyed (Keyed.ul / Keyed.ol) with a viewXItem function per list
style.externalEvents: one incoming port; Json.Decode into the app's messages (serverSet → the widget's Replaced, notify → the feed's Notified, tick → Tick calling each time-driven widget's tick, snapshot → GotSnapshot)
style.events: onInput for text inputs and the select, onClick for buttons and checkboxes, Ui.onNumberInput (an integer in range, else no message) for number inputs
style.formatting: as elm-format 0.8.8 writes it; elm.json lists only the dependencies the app imports
style.build: elm make --optimize, then uglify-js compress (pure_funcs) and mangle passes, as the Elm guide recommends

style.components: the form is one component (W1) in one file, a handler per message and one JSX tree, plus the companion (W2); no sub-components, no field table
style.state: one createStore for the whole page, shared through a context; widgets use path setters on their slice, produce for click messages; readers read other widgets' slices
style.externalEvents: store.receive(msg); serverSet and snapshot through reconcile(…, { key: 'id' }); tick written out per time-driven int
style.derived: plain expressions in the JSX, one fine-grained binding each
style.events: onClick/onInput (delegated), onChange for checkboxes and selects; number inputs send only integers within range
style.build: Vite + vite-plugin-solid, production defaults, hidden source maps

style.components: the form is one tag (settings-form) in one file, a <let> per field and one template, plus the companion tag; no sub-tags, no field table
style.state: each tag owns its fields as <let>s and <return>s an API (the form: the fields the companion reads, set, tick, notify; the companion: set); the root names the tags with tag variables and passes the companion the fields it reads
style.externalEvents: app.marko <return>s a router (a <const> in the page element, after the tags) that calls the tags' set, tick and notify; lists copied out of messages
style.lists: <for by="id">; immutable updates that find items by id
style.events: handlers in markup (onClick, valueChange, checkedChange); := for text inputs, checkboxes and selects; number inputs commit only integers within range, keeping an invalid edit in a local pending <let>
style.build: Vite + @marko/vite (linked: false), production mode, client-only mount, hidden source maps

style.track: prototype: no framework implements this strategy
style.components: the form is one module and the companion another, each written out from its own description; DOM built once from one static HTML string, elements referred to by their place in document order (E[n]); conditional sections swapped out by when while hidden; list rows built with createElement
style.messages: erased for DOM events: each update arm is inlined into the action its control calls, which writes the widget's fields in place
style.updates: each action schedules the per-field binding groups of the fields it writes (known at compile time); one microtask flush
style.derived: cross-widget reads register their bindings at mount in R.<widget>.<field>, only for fields some widget reads; the writing action schedules them
style.lists: keyed: add and remove schedule their row's edit, toggle its row's binding; other edits replace the array and reconcile by id in one forward pass
style.externalEvents: receive(msg): serverSet and snapshot replace a widget's state (a copy) and run all its bindings and its readers; tick and notify call the widgets' external arms
style.build: Vite with no framework plugin, production defaults, hidden source maps

style.architecture: The Elm Architecture: Tea.element, one Model record in Main, one update, one view (markup)
style.components: one module per widget (Model, init, Msg, update, view, replace; tick and notify where it needs them); Main only routes
style.routing: one Msg constructor per widget wrapping its Msg, plus Pushed for host events; Html.map in view
style.crossReads: a widget that reads earlier widgets takes their Models as extra arguments of view
style.conditional: if holes with an empty fragment
style.derived: expressions written out in the widget's view (interpolation or markup holes)
style.helpers: Ui: intIn (integer within limits) and shown (number input text), independent of every widget
style.externalEvents: project platform layer Push.onPush (Sub.on over a window event), read with a schema declaration and derived codecs
style.inputs: controlled inputs; an int with a number input keeps its typed text beside its last valid number

style.components: grain unit: the form is split into one instance per field unit (a field with its controls, displays and the bindings it adds), each in its own block of the page function (factory inlined, as it is called once): its slice of the one model, its own reducer (a table of arms by message tag, written out from its ops), template and bindings; the companion is an instance of its own; only generic helpers are shared
style.state: the form's one record is split into slices: each instance owns, in its closure, the fields of its unit; send(tag, value) runs its reducer arm and schedules that instance's binding list
style.updates: one patch function per instance, every DOM write skipped when unchanged; derived texts compiled to template literals; batched in a microtask
style.crossUnit: a binding that reads a field of another unit reads that instance's slice from the frame's registry in patch, and the reader watches the instance (follow); the companion reads the form the same way
style.combinedButtons: a combined button that writes a field of another unit: its own arm for its fields, and a message of its own for the other unit, sent after it (forward)
style.externalEvents: serverSet/snapshot of the form send every instance its Load message (it picks its own fields), the companion's are set; notify sends the feed's unit its Notify message; tick calls the instances of a shared running set, each subscribing while its gate is on
style.lists: runtime keyed list by item.id: patch changed rows, one forward placement pass when order or membership changes
style.dom: one static template per instance (a run of sibling nodes, trailing end tags left out), parsed in a fragment appended to the form, elements addressed by document order; one template per list row, cloned per new item
style.conditionals: node in the template; while hidden, an empty text node holds its place
style.events: tag 0 is Load; the template's controls take tags 1, 2, … in document order (then each row's controls), attached by position by the runtime's wire; messages are sent as send(tag, value); number inputs send valueAsNumber and the reducer takes integers within range only
style.build: Vite production build, no framework plugin, hidden source maps

style.components: one module per widget (bits, reducer, initial state, DOM factory with a static template whose bound elements are found by data-role, emptiness or a marker), each written from that widget's description; nothing interpreted at runtime
style.state: one immutable TEA model; the app reducer routes messages to the widgets' reducers
style.dirtyBits: words of 31 bits per widget, a field's number being the order the view first reads it; the dirty set is a sparse array of words; arms mark [word, bits, ...] at compile time; the app runs only the patches of the dirty words, so an event costs one word of bindings however big the form is; a group of bindings reading two words is a function each of those patches calls behind a test of both
style.updates: reducers are tables of arms by message tag; each arm returns the compile-time marks and values of the fields it writes, merged into the slice by the app; a static patch per word runs only the bindings whose bits are set, batched in a microtask
style.externalEvents: through the same reducer (send); serverSet and snapshot mark every word of the widgets they replace; tick goes to the time-driven widgets
style.crossWidgetReads: a reader has one bit per field it reads; the app patch sets it when the source's bit is dirty (one line per read)
style.lists: keyed by id: changed rows patched, gone rows removed, misplaced nodes moved in one walk
style.conditionals: branches (src/words.js) built once with the template, swapped for an empty comment while hidden, with their own nested patch testing the same words
style.events: addEventListener on each element; the handler builds a message and sends it
style.build: Vite with no framework plugin, production defaults, hidden source maps

compression.js: minified by the framework's production build

attribution: source maps: node_modules → runtime; unmapped bundler output → tooling (counted with runtime); the adapter file → adapter (excluded); everything else → app. Brotli split: runtime = brotli(runtime+tooling); app = brotli(app JS) − runtime.
